dedupe_keys.name: building resilient national ict infrastructure in asia and the pacific itu connect2recover framework and four country gap analysis 2025

description: This ITU study, produced under the Connect2Recover project with Australia's infrastructure department, develops a framework to assess the resilience of a country's ICT infrastructure and services and applies it in a gap analysis of four Asia-Pacific countries, among them Bhutan. The framework has four pillars with questions and indicators: network resilience, affordability of ICT, emergency preparedness, and early warning dissemination and communication. The report then lists good practices and case studies to close gaps, including non-terrestrial networks, infrastructure co-deployment and cell broadcasting (with a table of strengths and weaknesses). It finds Bhutan the most affordable of the four for mobile and fixed broadband while smartphones are expensive everywhere. Producer: ITU Asia-Pacific regional presence, with the Australian Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications; the 68-page PDF is a 2025 publication. Coverage: four countries in Asia and the Pacific, with least developed and small island states in focus. Access: free PDF on the ITU site. Licence and cost: free to read; licence not stated. Caveats: the other three countries' details were not read in full, and scores are assessments, not measurements. Simulation uses: the framework and gap findings support resilience and emergency-response scenario design for national ICT systems. Related records: none linked.
